Q: Neutralino Window PID A:

The "pid" Neutralino gives you isn't a real Windows process ID. It's just an internal ID that Neutralino made up.

When you create a new window, it's not a separate process. It's just another view inside the same Neutralino process. So there's only one real PID for your whole app. Those separate entries you see in Task Manager are WebView2 child processes, and Neutralino can't see them.

Your workaround (searching by window title) is actually what most people end up doing. Don't overthink it.

Alternatively, just save the window object when you create it and use Neutralino.window.close(win) instead of messing with taskkill at all. Works fine.

Q: pointermove vs. mousemove (apart from additional features) A:

Only pointermove (not mousemove) gets dispatched when a pointer changes "button state, pressure, tilt, or contact geometry (e.g. width and height)" even if clientX and clientY don't change.

mousemove - triggers when the focus is on the element being listened to.
pointermove - the event is fired when the pointer's coordinates change. In other words, whenever the pointer moves.
But in the end, pointermove is inherited from mousemove.
Simply put, mousemove handles the cursor coordinates, while pointermove handles the coordinates of the point of its projection onto the element. Otherwise, they are identical.

In this case, focus does not refer to the element's activity, but rather to the cursor position on the element being tracked.

The pointermove event is a derivative of mousemove. It is designed to work with touch screens. If you use a regular mouse, there will be no difference, except that the event will trigger the first time the pointer is shifted after the projection point (shadow) of the pointer appears on the tracked element (mousemove is triggered when the pointer touches your input). This is because using pointermove is aimed at determining not only the position of the pointer, but also the size of its projection, the shape of the pointer, how hard the user pressed on the screen and the type of device used to process this pressure. After that, ponmtermove calls mousemove and outputs the coordinates of the upper-left corner of the pointer projection. It works the same on all browsers, the only difference is in the indentation of the pointer block itself.

Sequence:

  • You have touched the touch screen with your finger. The area of the touch (projection) is 1px*1px -> the Mousemove event was triggered. The coordinates of the touch point X and Y are obtained.

  • You pressed the screen harder -> the touch area increased -> the Pointermove event was triggered.

  • You pressed harder on the screen -> the footprint area became larger -> Pointermove again.

  • You pressed the screen unevenly and in some way the fingerprint became larger relative to the first touch point -> the Dragmove event was triggered.

When requesting e.clientX/e.clientY, you will get the X/Y coordinates of the first touch received by Mousemove.

On a normal screen, the cursor coordinates are always equal to the coordinates of the upper-left corner of the pointer, so no matter which handler you bind, the result will always be mousemove.

Q: Why does my pandas groupby() result not show total sales by product correctly? A: 
result = df.groupby("product")["sales"].sum()
print(result)

code：

import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "product": ["apple", "banana", "apple", "orange", "banana"],
    "quantity": [2, 3, 1, 5, 2],
    "price": [3, 2, 3, 4, 2]
})

df["sales"] = df["quantity"] * df["price"]

result = df.groupby("product")["sales"].sum()

print(result)

Output:

product
apple      9
banana    10
orange    20
Name: sales, dtype: int64That 



result = df.groupby("product")["sales"]

只创建了一个 SeriesGroupBy object。
groupby() 本身只是把数据“按 product 分组”，但还没有告诉 pandas 对每一组做什么操作。

你需要在后面加一个 aggregation method，比如：

.sum()

意思是：对每个 product 分组后的 sales 求和。

所以正确写法是：

df.groupby("product")["sales"].sum()

更完整地说：

df["sales"] = df["quantity"] * df["price"]
result = df.groupby("product")["sales"].sum()

Q: How do I cache images in local storage? A:

You generally should not cache local images manually in LocalStorage / RAM if the files already exist on disk.

For Android image apps, the best practice is:

  • Store the original image on disk (which you already do)

  • Generate and cache thumbnails/previews, not the full-resolution image

  • Load scaled images into the UI using Coil/Glide

Right now the real problem is probably that you're loading the full-resolution images (several hundred MB) into the album grid/list. Even SSD storage becomes slow with files that large.

Best approach:

AsyncImage(
    model = ImageRequest.Builder(context)
        .data(file)
        .size(300) // thumbnail size
        .crossfade(true)
        .build(),
    contentDescription = null
)

or with Coil:

.allowHardware(true)
.memoryCachePolicy(CachePolicy.ENABLED)
.diskCachePolicy(CachePolicy.ENABLED)

Also:

  • Use thumbnails for album pages

  • Load original image only when user opens the photo

  • Consider generating thumbnails once and saving them in a .thumbnails folder

  • Coil does cache local images, but caching huge originals is inefficient and may be skipped depending on request size/configuration

If images are really “hundreds of MB”, you should also check:

  • image compression

  • bitmap sampling (inSampleSize)

  • HEIF/WebP/JPEG quality settings

Loading gigantic originals into RecyclerView/Grid is usually the main bottleneck.
